stack_lifetimes: 15 caller-stack slots are fixed size, allocated in syscall/transfer frames; frame stays alive across synchronous family calls and blocking waits.
Unix ring writes/reads and address copies complete while frame remains alive; inet TCP uses COPY, UDP pbuf_take, netlink copies synchronously. No family retains scratch/header pointer.
Original zero fills/0xff sentinels/whole MsgHdr zero initialization are preserved. Heap buffer allocation/free path for messages larger than 512 remains unchanged.
fd_queue_ownership: collect_passed_fds owns acquired FD references; group.fds << fds allocates one independent backing array containing those pointers.
Both unsafe appends move that backing array header into the queue; emitted C uses plain struct assignment followed by array_push, never a clone. Success frees sender pointer metadata only.

Error, full-queue timeout/cancellation, invalid target, EPIPE and oversize exits occur before group allocation/enqueue; caller releases the original references. No fallible return follows queue transfer.
Receive installs accepted FD references in the process table; rejected/truncated/pledge-denied/failed installation references are unreferenced. The queue metadata is freed once and group removed.
Plain reads, record truncation and endpoint close unreference all undelivered refs, free group metadata once and remove/detach queue. Existing group locals and close iteration are shallow C copies.
Endpoint locks serialize append with reads/close; pending array is noslices and no group metadata is sliced, so queue reallocation can free old queue backing.
